title: Why Opportunities & Pipelines Matter
learningGoal: Understand why leads get lost and how Opportunities and Pipelines help prevent that.

items.title: The Problem
items.description: Most leads are not lost because someone said no. They are often lost because: Nobody followed up. The lead stayed buried in the inbox. The business owner forgot the next step. There was no clear sales process. The lead was interested, but nobody tracked the opportunity.

items.title: The Solution
items.description: LeadProspectrr helps fix this by giving you a clear place to track who is interested and where they are in the process.

items.title: The Inbox Shows Conversation
items.description: Conversations are where messages happen.

items.title: The Pipeline Shows Business Status
items.description: Opportunities are where possible business is tracked. Pipelines show the path each lead moves through.

items.title: Speaker Receives Message
items.description: Hi, I saw your post about helping speakers follow up after events. I would like to know more about how that works.

items.title: What Should Happen
items.description: That person should not just stay in the inbox. They should be added as an Opportunity so they can be followed up with properly.

keyPoint: If someone could become a client, they should be tracked as an Opportunity. The inbox shows conversation; the pipeline shows business status.

actionSteps.title: Think of a Recent Lead
actionSteps.description: Think of one person who recently showed interest in your service.

actionSteps.title: Ask Yourself
actionSteps.description: Are they currently tracked somewhere? Do I know their next step? Could I find them quickly today?

actionSteps.title: Identify the Gap
actionSteps.description: If you cannot answer yes to all three questions, you need Opportunities and Pipelines.

quizzes.question: Why do most leads get lost?

options.option_text: Because nobody followed up, the lead stayed in inbox, or the next step was forgotten
Because the price was too high

quizzes.explanation: Most leads are lost due to lack of follow-up, not because of price or interest. They get buried in the inbox or the next step is forgotten.

quizzes.question: What does the pipeline show?

options.option_text: Business status and where leads are in the sales process

quizzes.explanation: The pipeline shows business status - where each lead stands in the sales process. The inbox shows conversations, but the pipeline shows the sales journey.

quizzes.question: What should happen when someone shows interest?

options.option_text: Let them stay in the inbox
Add them as an Opportunity for proper follow-up
Wait for them to contact again

quizzes.explanation: When someone shows interest, they should be added as an Opportunity so they can be properly tracked and followed up with, not left in the inbox.

title: What Is an Opportunity?
learningGoal: Understand what an Opportunity is and when to create one.

items.title: An Opportunity Is
items.description: A lead, contact, or business that could become a client. It is not just a name in your contacts. It is someone who has shown some kind of interest.

items.title: Form Submissions
items.description: They fill out a form asking about your services.

items.title: Booked Calls
items.description: They book a call or consultation.

items.title: Pricing Inquiries
items.description: They ask for pricing or a quote.

items.title: Replies and Questions
items.description: They reply to a text or email, or ask about a service.

items.title: Downloads with Interest
items.description: They download a guide and show interest.

items.title: Coach
items.description: Someone downloads a leadership guide and replies asking about private coaching.

items.title: Consultant
items.description: A business owner asks for help fixing a messy sales process.

items.title: Speaker
items.description: An event planner asks about availability and speaking fees.

items.title: Trainer
items.description: A company asks about a team workshop.

items.title: Key Information
items.description: Who the lead is, what they are interested in, where they are in the sales process, what the possible value is, what happened last, what needs to happen next.

keyPoint: A contact is a person. An Opportunity is a possible sale, project, booking, or client relationship. Create Opportunities when someone shows interest in becoming a client.

actionSteps.title: List Potential Opportunities
actionSteps.description: Write down three people who could be added as Opportunities in your business.

actionSteps.title: Identify Interest Signals
actionSteps.description: What did they do that showed interest? (Form, call booking, pricing question, etc.)

actionSteps.title: Plan Next Steps
actionSteps.description: For each person, what would be the next step if they were an Opportunity?

quizzes.question: What is an Opportunity?

options.option_text: Just a name in your contacts
A lead, contact, or business that could become a client

quizzes.explanation: An Opportunity is a lead, contact, or business that could become a client. It represents possible business, not just a contact name.

quizzes.question: When should you create an Opportunity?

options.option_text: When they show interest by filling out a form, booking a call, asking for pricing, or inquiring about services

quizzes.explanation: Create an Opportunity when someone shows interest in becoming a client - through form submissions, call bookings, pricing inquiries, or service questions.

quizzes.question: What information does an Opportunity help you track?

options.option_text: Who the lead is, what they want, where they are in the process, the value, what happened, and what's next

quizzes.explanation: An Opportunity tracks comprehensive information: who the lead is, what they are interested in, their stage in the sales process, possible value, recent activity, and next steps.

title: What Is a Pipeline?
learningGoal: Understand how a Pipeline works and why it makes follow-up easier.

items.title: The Path
items.description: A Pipeline is the path a lead moves through from first interest to a final decision. Think of it as a row of buckets. Each bucket shows where the lead is right now.

items.title: 1. New Lead
items.description: Someone has shown interest, but no real follow-up has happened yet.

items.title: 2. Contacted
items.description: You have replied, called, texted, or emailed the lead.

items.title: 3. Appointment Booked
items.description: The lead has booked a call, consultation, meeting, or session.

items.title: 4. Proposal Sent
items.description: You have sent pricing, a proposal, agreement, or next-step details.

items.title: 5. Won
items.description: The person has agreed to move forward.

items.title: 6. Lost
items.description: The person is not moving forward right now.

items.title: Lost Is Not Failure
items.description: Lost does not mean failure. It simply means the lead is no longer active in this pipeline. They may re-engage later or be better suited for a different offer.

keyPoint: A Pipeline gives you a visual way to see where every lead stands. It is like a row of buckets - each lead sits in the bucket that matches their current status.

actionSteps.title: Review the Stages
actionSteps.description: Look at the six stages: New Lead, Contacted, Appointment Booked, Proposal Sent, Won, Lost.

actionSteps.title: Adapt for Your Business
actionSteps.description: Would these stages work for your business, or do you need one or two different names?

actionSteps.title: Define Your Stages
actionSteps.description: Write down the 4-6 stages that match your sales process.

quizzes.question: What is a Pipeline?

options.option_text: The path a lead moves through from first interest to final decision

quizzes.explanation: A Pipeline is the path a lead moves through from first interest to final decision. It visualizes the sales journey with stages like New Lead, Contacted, Appointment Booked, etc.

quizzes.question: What does the 'Lost' stage mean?

options.option_text: The lead is not moving forward right now in this pipeline
The lead should be deleted forever
You should never contact them again

quizzes.explanation: Lost does not mean failure. It simply means the lead is not moving forward in this pipeline right now. They may re-engage later or be suited for a different offer.

quizzes.question: Which stage comes after 'Contacted'?
quizzes.explanation: The typical flow is: New Lead → Contacted → Appointment Booked → Proposal Sent → Won/Lost. After Contacted comes Appointment Booked.

items.title: Take Your Time

keyPoint: The Opportunities area is the visual board that helps you see possible business at a glance. It shows leads as cards in different pipeline stages.

quizzes.question: Where does sales tracking live in LeadProspectrr?

quizzes.question: What can you see on the Opportunities board?

quizzes.explanation: The Opportunities board shows: pipeline name, stage columns, lead cards, contact names, opportunity value, status, notes, assigned user, and stage movement options.

quizzes.question: What question can the board help you answer?

title: Creating a Sample Opportunity
learningGoal: Learn how to create an Opportunity using a simple example.

items.title: Sarah Johnson
items.description: Name: Sarah Johnson. Interest: Website redesign. Estimated Value: $2,500. Current Stage: New Lead. Next Step: Book a call.

items.title: 1-3. Navigate
items.description: Go to Opportunities area. Choose correct Pipeline. Add new Opportunity.

items.title: 4-5. Contact Details
items.description: Select or create contact. Add Opportunity name.

items.title: 6-7. Value and Stage
items.description: Add estimated value. Choose correct stage.

items.title: 8-9. Note and Save
items.description: Add short note. Save the Opportunity.

items.title: Good Note
items.description: Sarah asked about a website redesign. Needs a short discovery call to understand project scope and timeline.

items.title: Does Not Need to Be Perfect
items.description: The estimated value does not have to be perfect. It helps you understand possible revenue in the pipeline.

keyPoint: Creating an Opportunity gives a lead a clear place in your sales process. Include contact details, value, stage, and notes for proper tracking.

actionSteps.title: Create Sample Opportunity
actionSteps.description: Use Sarah Johnson example or create your own sample lead.

actionSteps.title: Fill All Fields
actionSteps.description: Add name, value, stage, and a descriptive note.

actionSteps.title: Save and Verify
actionSteps.description: Save the Opportunity and confirm it appears in the correct stage.

quizzes.question: What is the first step in creating an Opportunity?
quizzes.explanation: The first step is to go to the Opportunities area in LeadProspectrr, then choose the correct pipeline and add a new Opportunity.

quizzes.question: Why add an estimated value to an Opportunity?

options.option_text: It helps you understand possible revenue in the pipeline

quizzes.explanation: The estimated value helps you understand possible revenue in your pipeline. It does not need to be perfect - it is for tracking and forecasting purposes.

quizzes.question: What should a good note include?

options.option_text: Details about what they want, project scope, and next steps
Your personal opinions about the lead

quizzes.explanation: A good note includes details about what the lead asked for, project scope, timeline, and next steps. Example: 'Sarah asked about website redesign. Needs discovery call to understand scope and timeline.'

title: Moving Leads Through the Pipeline
learningGoal: Learn how and when to move an Opportunity from one stage to another.

items.title: Move When Something Changes
items.description: A lead should move when something changes. Contacted them? Move to Contacted. They booked a call? Move to Appointment Booked. Sent proposal? Move to Proposal Sent. They said yes? Move to Won. Not moving forward? Move to Lost.

items.title: 1. New Lead
items.description: Sarah asked about a website redesign.

items.title: 2. Contacted
items.description: You replied and asked her to book a call.

items.title: 3. Appointment Booked
items.description: Sarah booked a discovery call.

items.title: 4. Proposal Sent
items.description: You sent her the website proposal.

items.title: 5. Won
items.description: Sarah accepted and paid the deposit.

items.title: Visual Clarity
items.description: Moving cards through the pipeline helps you avoid guessing. You can look at the board and know what needs attention.

keyPoint: Move the Opportunity card whenever the sales status changes. This keeps your pipeline accurate and shows you exactly what needs attention.

actionSteps.title: Review Current Opportunities
actionSteps.description: Look at your Opportunities and identify which ones need to move stages.

actionSteps.title: Move One Lead
actionSteps.description: Take one example lead and move them to the correct stage based on what has happened.

actionSteps.title: Update Notes
actionSteps.description: Add a note about why you moved them and what happened.

quizzes.question: When should you move a lead to the 'Contacted' stage?

options.option_text: When you have replied, called, texted, or emailed them

quizzes.explanation: Move a lead to Contacted when you have actively reached out to them - by replying, calling, texting, or emailing. This shows the lead has been contacted, not just that they showed interest.

quizzes.question: Why is moving leads through the pipeline important?

options.option_text: It makes the board look colorful
It helps you avoid guessing and know what needs attention

quizzes.explanation: Moving leads through the pipeline gives you visual clarity. You can look at the board and immediately know what needs attention - who is new, who has been contacted, who needs a proposal, etc.

quizzes.question: What should you do when a lead says yes to your offer?
quizzes.explanation: When a lead agrees to move forward and becomes a client, move them to the 'Won' stage. This tracks your successful conversions and clears them from active follow-up stages.

title: Adding Notes and Next Steps
learningGoal: Understand why notes and next steps are part of good follow-up.

items.title: Stage + Note + Next Step
items.description: A pipeline stage tells you where the lead is. A note tells you what happened. A next step tells you what to do next. You need all three.

items.title: What to Record
items.description: What the lead asked for. What service they are interested in. What was discussed. Any deadline or event date. Any pricing concern. The next promised action.

items.title: Bad Note
items.description: Spoke to her. (Too vague - no useful information)

items.title: Better Note
items.description: Spoke with Sarah about website redesign. She wants a cleaner site and better lead capture. Send proposal by Thursday and follow up Monday if no reply.

items.title: Common Next Steps
items.description: Send proposal. Book consultation. Follow up in 3 days. Send payment link. Ask for event date. Send case study.

keyPoint: A lead without a note and next step is easy to forget. Always record what happened and what needs to happen next.

actionSteps.title: Review Your Opportunities
actionSteps.description: Look at your current Opportunities and check if they have notes.

actionSteps.title: Add a Note
actionSteps.description: Add a short, descriptive note to one Opportunity with details about what was discussed.

actionSteps.title: Set Next Step
actionSteps.description: Add a clear next step so you know what to do next.

quizzes.question: What three things do you need for good follow-up?
quizzes.explanation: You need three things: the pipeline stage (where they are), a note (what happened), and a next step (what to do next). All three are essential for good follow-up.

quizzes.question: What makes a good note?

options.option_text: Details about what they want, what was discussed, deadlines, and next actions

quizzes.explanation: A good note includes details: what the lead asked for, what service they want, what was discussed, any deadlines, pricing concerns, and the next promised action.

quizzes.question: Why are next steps important?

options.option_text: A lead without a next step is easy to forget

quizzes.explanation: Next steps are crucial because a lead without a defined next action is easy to forget. Clear next steps ensure consistent follow-up.

title: Daily Pipeline Check-In
learningGoal: Build a simple habit for keeping the pipeline clean and useful.

items.title: Pipeline Only Works If Checked
items.description: Your pipeline only works if you check it regularly. This does not need to take long. A five-minute check-in can stop leads from being forgotten.

items.title: 8-Step Routine
items.description: 1. Open Opportunities. 2. Review New Leads. 3. Review Contacted leads. 4. Check Appointment Booked. 5. Check Proposal Sent. 6. Move anything that has changed. 7. Add notes where needed. 8. Set the next follow-up action.

items.title: Choose a Regular Time
items.description: Start of the day. After lunch. End of the day. Choose one regular time each workday.

items.title: Never Close Without Next Step
items.description: Never close the pipeline if an active lead has no next step.

keyPoint: A simple daily review keeps your follow-up under control. Choose a regular time and never close the pipeline if an active lead has no next step.

actionSteps.title: Choose Your Time
actionSteps.description: Choose a daily time for your pipeline check-in (start of day, after lunch, or end of day).

actionSteps.title: Set a Reminder
actionSteps.description: Set a calendar reminder or alarm for your daily check-in.

actionSteps.title: Do First Check-In
actionSteps.description: Complete your first 8-step check-in today.

quizzes.question: How long should a daily pipeline check-in take?
quizzes.explanation: A daily pipeline check-in only takes about five minutes. This short time investment prevents leads from being forgotten.

quizzes.question: What is the simple rule for closing the pipeline?

options.option_text: Never close the pipeline if an active lead has no next step
Only check it once per month

quizzes.explanation: The simple rule: Never close the pipeline if an active lead has no next step. This ensures every lead has a defined follow-up action.

quizzes.question: What should you do during the daily check-in?

options.option_text: Review all stages, move changed leads, add notes, set next actions

quizzes.explanation: During the daily check-in: review New Leads, Contacted, Appointment Booked, Proposal Sent; move anything that changed; add notes; set next follow-up actions.

title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
learningGoal: Avoid the habits that make pipelines messy and hard to use.

items.title: Keep It Simple
items.description: Too many stages makes the pipeline confusing. Keep it simple with 4-6 clear stages.

items.title: Move When Status Changes
items.description: If the lead has changed status, the card should move. Don't leave leads in the wrong stage.

items.title: Move to Lost When Appropriate
items.description: If someone is not moving forward, move them to Lost or another inactive stage. Don't clutter active stages.

items.title: Always Add Notes
items.description: Without notes, you may not remember what happened. Always record key information.

sections.title: Mistake 5: Using Inbox as Sales Tracker

items.title: Inbox vs Pipeline
items.description: The inbox is for messages. The pipeline is for sales status. Don't confuse the two.

items.title: Check Regularly
items.description: A pipeline that is not checked becomes another forgotten system. Daily check-ins are essential.

keyPoint: A clean pipeline is easier to use and more likely to bring in business. Avoid too many stages, not moving leads, leaving old leads active, forgetting notes, using inbox as tracker, and not checking regularly.

actionSteps.title: Review Your Pipeline
actionSteps.description: Look at your current pipeline for any of these six mistakes.

actionSteps.title: Identify One Fix
actionSteps.description: Find one mistake you can clean up today.

actionSteps.title: Make the Fix
actionSteps.description: Take action to correct the identified mistake.

quizzes.question: What is Mistake 1 to avoid?
quizzes.explanation: Mistake 1 is creating too many stages. Too many stages makes the pipeline confusing. Keep it simple with 4-6 clear stages.

quizzes.question: Why should you not use the inbox as your sales tracker?

options.option_text: The inbox is for messages; the pipeline is for sales status

quizzes.explanation: The inbox is for messages and conversations. The pipeline is for tracking sales status. They serve different purposes - don't confuse them.

quizzes.question: What should you do with old leads who are not moving forward?

options.option_text: Leave them in active stages forever
Move them to Lost or inactive stages

quizzes.explanation: If someone is not moving forward, move them to Lost or another inactive stage. This keeps your active pipeline clean and focused on real opportunities.

items.title: Q4: What next action?
